title: Web forms and files (safe handling)
learningObjectives: Explain web forms and files (safe handling) and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: Forms expose values through controls and FormData. File inputs provide File objects that can be inspected for metadata and read through suitable APIs. The accept attribute is a user-interface hint, not a security boundary; server-side validation and safe storage are still required.
understand.whyItMatters: File names, MIME types, and client checks can be spoofed. Limit file size and type on the server, avoid trusting client metadata, and do not render untrusted file contents as HTML.
understand.analogy: A file input is a submission tray; checking the label on the tray does not prove what is inside the package.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: FormData collects submitted control values. This example reads metadata only and does not upload or trust the file.

examples.explanation: FormData collects submitted control values. This example reads metadata only and does not upload or trust the file.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates the API or security principle; browser permission or environment support may be required.

practise.guidedTask: Build a file picker that displays selected file name and size, rejects oversized files in the UI, and documents why the server must validate again.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: Does the HTML accept attribute securely validate uploaded file types?
options: No, it is only a selection hint
questions.answer: No, it is only a selection hint
questions.explanation: The accept attribute guides the file picker but does not replace server-side validation.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
